contract: A writer may commit only under the exact current monotonically increasing lease generation for the key. Worker names are reusable after restart. Read and write values are atomic in this in-memory store; the lease check and mutation occur synchronously in commit.

evidenceRequirements.description: Explain how the supplied guard preserves its contract across relevant ownership/time boundaries. Do not require knowledge of an unseen sibling. Evaluator counterfactual only: Worker name w acquires generation 1 and prepares old data. After expiry the same name acquires generation 2 and commits new data. The generation-1 completion still passes name equality and overwrites new data. Comparing token generation at commit rejects it.

Explain at least one relevant boundary or benign path inferable from the supplied code/context; the following evaluator examples are alternatives, not a mandatory unseen checklist: A current token commits; a different owner is rejected; same-name restart must be distinguished; repeated current commits are permitted by the supplied contract.

forbiddenClaims: Production outage, real data exfiltration or universal safety without supplied evidence.
A missing contract establishes either a definite defect or unconditional protection.
Simulated time or offline passing tests establish real scheduler/OS behavior or model improvement.
independence: non-independent, same-workflow authorship and public artifacts
